correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined 12-vertex 30-edge icosahedral graph, the recursive matching enumeration exhausts each state exactly once by matching the least remaining vertex. Every possible pair is checked for legal 4/6-cycle symmetric difference; independently a dual dodecahedral construction enumerates all simple 4/6-cycles and toggles them. Both programs assert 125 states, 300 four-flip edges, 580 six-flip edges, six 4-flip components sized 120+5, exact edge partition by five frozen states, 880 total edges and the full distance degree profiles. BFS from every vertex certifies eccentricity 3 and the sharp cutoff. All assertions passed on extracted actual source programs.

value.rationale: This is a natural sharp local-transformation threshold on a canonical five-regular Platonic graph: length four strands precisely five configurations, but length six connects all, with complete 125-state exact transition geometry and a uniform diameter three. The five frozen perfect matchings recover a classical symmetric 1-factorization dynamically, and precise degree/distance distributions quantify mobility rather than merely reproducing a known matching count. The finite object is structurally canonical, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
